ai.title: System prompt file request step moved second
ai.summary: The file request step is moved from position 0 to position 2 in the `getResponseFormatPrompt` function. A dynamic `bulletNumber` counter now handles step numbering instead of hardcoded values. This change affects the general case workflow for file context updates in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: The instructions the assistant follows for handling file requests have been reordered so the file request now happens second instead of first. This means the assistant reads the files it currently has, then asks for any additional files before moving on to the next steps. The step numbers now update automatically instead of being fixed, making it easier to adjust the order in the future.

ai.title: Catch errors in deadConnectionCleaner loop
ai.summary: Added a try/catch block around the client iteration in the `deadConnectionCleaner` interval in `backend/src/websockets/server.ts`. Previously, an error thrown by `SWITCHBOARD.getClient` would propagate and crash the interval, halting connection cleanup. Now, errors are logged to the console, allowing the cleaner to continue running.

eli5.text: The system now handles unexpected glitches that happened while checking for inactive connections, so background cleanup keeps running instead of stopping mid-check. If you rely on live connections, you would notice that stale sessions are now removed more reliably because the cleanup process no longer stops when it hits an error. This is already active today.

ai.title: Add debug log for new file content in diff expansion
ai.summary: Added debugLog call in backend/src/generate-diffs-via-expansion.ts to log unexpanded new file content. This change aids in debugging diff generation issues by providing visibility into the raw content before expansion. The update is internal and does not affect user-facing behavior.

eli5.text: The people who maintain the system's behind-the-scenes file comparison tools added a hidden note-taking feature while they work. When the assistant creates a new file, the system now quietly saves a copy of the original content before it changes it, so if something goes wrong during the editing process, they can look back and see exactly what the file looked like beforehand. You won't see this anywhere, but it helps the development team fix problems faster when the assistant's edits don't turn out right.

ai.title: Propagate WebSocket errors to CLI state
ai.summary: APIRealtimeClient now accepts an onError callback, invoked on first connection failure. CLI constructs Client internally and binds onWebSocketError to halt loading animations and reset isReceivingResponse before printing retry message. Scope covers common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts, npm-app/src/client.ts, npm-app/src/cli.ts, and npm-app/src/index.ts. Refactor moves Client and ChatStorage instantiation from index.ts into CLI constructor, coupling connect() with readyPromise.

eli5.text: When the app fails to connect to the internet (like a dropped call), it now tells you in plain yellow text 'Could not connect. Retrying...' instead of just hanging silently with a spinning animation. You'll see the typing indicator stop immediately, and the message appears right away. This fix is live today for all users of the main application.

ai.title: System prompt emphasizes file requests
ai.summary: The system prompt in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` was updated to explicitly instruct the model to use the `update_file_context` tool for requesting files. The logic now prioritizes checking for missing files before assuming sufficiency, changing the confirmation text from a passive check to an active request directive. This applies to the core backend system prompt generation.

eli5.text: If you interact with the coding assistant, you may now notice that it more actively asks you to let it pull in files it needs to complete a task. Previously, the instruction it received was more passive, essentially checking whether it had all the required files. Now, the guidance explicitly tells it to request missing files using a specific tool, and to double-check its assumptions rather than just confirming it has everything. This makes the assistant more likely to fetch and review relevant files on its own before proceeding, rather than assuming it already has what it needs.

ai.title: Add bun-types to backend and root tsconfig
ai.summary: Added bun-types ^1.1.25 to devDependencies in backend/package.json and root package.json. Updated backend/tsconfig.json types array to include bun-types alongside node and jest. This enables TypeScript to resolve Bun-specific global types and APIs.

eli5.text: The app now knows about a newer kind of tool kit (Bun) that its builders use to run parts of the system, so the helper programs that check and prepare your experience can read it without confusion. Only the people building the app are affected; if you peeked at the setup files you'd see a new entry added to the list of tools the system is allowed to understand.
